Eligibility & Policy Term

The LIC New Children's Money Back Plan (UIN: 512N296V02) is designed for children from birth (0 years) up to 12 years of age. The policy term is fixed to mature when the child turns 25. For example, if you buy the plan for a 5-year-old child, the policy term will be 20 years (25 - 5). For the official details, see the official brochure.

content.text: This plan is excellent for parents who want a disciplined, 'set-it-and-forget-it' approach. The fixed payouts are perfectly timed for major educational expenses. However, its rigidity is also its weakness; you cannot alter this payout schedule.

sections.title: Deep Dive: LIC Jeevan Tarun â€” The Flexibility Champion

content.text:
Jeevan Tarun (UIN: 512N292V02) is unique because it offers four different options for receiving survival benefits between the ages of 20 and 24, making it highly suitable for funding higher education. You can choose to receive a percentage of the sum assured annually or let it accumulate. Surrender and loan facilities are available after two full years of premium payment. Refer to the Jeevan Tarun brochure for more. For comprehensive retirement planning alongside child education, compare with our NPS Calculator.

LIC Jeevan Tarun Options Explained

This plan's main advantage is its flexibility. At the time of proposal, you must choose one of four options for how the survival benefits are paid out:

  • Option 1: No survival benefit. Receive 100% of the Sum Assured + bonuses at maturity (age 25).
  • Option 2: Receive 5% of the Sum Assured every year from age 20 to 24. At maturity, receive the remaining 75% of the Sum Assured + bonuses.
  • Option 3: Receive 10% of the Sum Assured every year from age 20 to 24. At maturity, receive the remaining 50% of the Sum Assured + bonuses.
  • Option 4: Receive 15% of the Sum Assured every year from age 20 to 24. At maturity, receive the remaining 25% of the Sum Assured + bonuses.

sections.title: Deep Dive: LIC Amritbaal (Plan 874) â€” A Modern Approach

content.text:
LIC Amritbaal Plan 874 Details

LIC Amritbaal is a non-participating, non-linked, individual savings life insurance plan designed for children. Unlike traditional money-back plans, its primary focus is to build a guaranteed lump-sum amount for a future date.

Key Features & Eligibility

  • Entry Age: 30 days to 13 years.
  • Guaranteed Additions: A key feature is the Guaranteed Additions of â‚¹80 per thousand Basic Sum Assured, which accrue at the end of each policy year and are paid out at maturity. This provides a clear, predictable growth path.
  • Maturity: The plan matures when the child reaches an age between 18 and 25, as chosen by the proposer.
  • Payment Options: It offers both Single Premium and Limited Premium payment options (5, 6, or 7 years).

Amritbaal vs Jeevan Tarun: Corpus Building vs Staggered Payouts

The main difference between Amritbaal and plans like Jeevan Tarun or the Children's Money Back Plan is its structure. Amritbaal is built to deliver a single, substantial lump sum at maturity, enhanced by guaranteed additions. In contrast, the other plans are designed to provide staggered 'money-back' payments at specific milestones. Amritbaal is better for those who prefer to receive the entire corpus in one go for a major expense like post-graduate studies abroad or a wedding, rather than smaller, periodic payouts.

content.text: My Take: If you want absolute peace of mind and are primarily looking for a safe savings tool, an LIC plan is unbeatable. If you have a higher risk appetite and are aiming for inflation-beating growth over 15+ years, a well-chosen ULIP could potentially generate a much larger corpus for your child.

Premiums paid for LIC child plans are eligible for deduction under Section 80C, and maturity/death benefits are generally tax-free under Section 10(10D), subject to conditions. You can add riders like Premium Waiver Benefit, which is highly recommended. Nomination is a straightforward process to ensure the benefit goes to the right person.

items.q: Which LIC child plan is best for education?
items.a: For flexible higher education funding between ages 20-24, Jeevan Tarun (934) is excellent. For staggered payouts for milestones like 12th grade and college years (ages 18, 20, 22), the New Childrenâ€™s Money Back Plan (932) is ideal. For a simple, guaranteed lump sum at a specific age, Amritbaal (874) is the best choice.

items.q: Which is better â€” LIC Jeevan Tarun or New Childrenâ€™s Money Back?
items.a: Jeevan Tarun is better for flexibility, allowing you to choose how and if you receive payouts between ages 20 and 24. The New Children's Money Back Plan has a fixed, rigid payout schedule at ages 18, 20, and 22. Choose Tarun if you want more control over the money flow for higher education.

Amritbaal is a non-participating endowment plan focused on providing a guaranteed lump sum for a child's future. Unlike other plans, its returns are not based on variable bonuses but on Guaranteed Additions (â‚¹80 per â‚¹1000 SA) that accrue each year, making the final maturity amount highly predictable.

items.q: Is LIC child plan good for daughters?
items.a: Yes, LIC child plans are an excellent and safe way to save for a daughter's education and marriage. They provide guaranteed returns and insurance cover. You can also compare these plans with the government's Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY), which currently offers a higher, tax-free interest rate specifically for a girl child.

items.q: What happens if parent dies in LIC child plan?
items.a: If the parent (proposer) has opted for the Premium Waiver Benefit (PWB) rider, all future premiums are waived upon their death, but the policy benefits for the child continue uninterrupted. Without this rider, the family would need to continue paying premiums to keep the policy active.

items.q: Can I surrender LIC child plan early?
items.a: Yes, you can surrender the policy after it acquires a surrender value, typically after paying premiums for two full years. However, surrendering early results in a significant financial loss. It is generally better to make the policy 'Paid-Up' with reduced benefits if you can no longer pay premiums.

items.q: Is LIC child plan better than ULIP for children?
items.a: It depends on your risk appetite. LIC child plans offer guaranteed, safe returns. ULIPs (Unit Linked Insurance Plans) invest in the market and have the potential for much higher returns, but they also carry market risk and do not offer guarantees. Choose LIC for safety and ULIPs for higher growth potential.

items.q: Does LIC child plan give loan facility?
items.a: Yes, most LIC child plans, including Jeevan Tarun and New Children's Money Back, offer a loan facility once the policy has acquired a surrender value (typically after 2-3 years of premium payments). This allows for liquidity without terminating the policy.

items.q: How to calculate LIC child plan maturity value?
items.a: The maturity value is typically the Sum Assured + Vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses + Final Additional Bonus (FAB). Our calculator provides a close estimate by using illustrative bonus rates based on historical performance.

items.q: What tax benefits are available under LIC child plan 2025?
items.a: Premiums paid (up to â‚¹1.5 lakh) are eligible for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. The maturity amount and survival benefits received are generally tax-free under Section 10(10D), provided the annual premium does not exceed 10% of the sum assured.

items.q: How does LIC child plan compare with other investment options?
items.a: LIC child plans offer guaranteed returns with insurance cover. Compare with PPF for tax-free savings, FD vs PPF for fixed deposits, or mutual funds for market-linked growth.
